nodes.Name: pattern
nodes.DocComment:
A pattern is something that can be matched against an HTTP request.
It has an optional method, an optional host, and a path.

Fields.Name: loc
Fields.DocComment: source location of registering call, for helpful messages

nodes.Name: segment

Fields.Name: s
Fields.DocComment: literal or wildcard name or "/" for "/{$}".

nodes.Name: parsePattern
nodes.DocComment:
parsePattern parses a string into a Pattern.
The string's syntax is

	[METHOD] [HOST]/[PATH]

where:
  - METHOD is an HTTP method
  - HOST is a hostname
  - PATH consists of slash-separated segments, where each segment is either
    a literal or a wildcard of the form "{name}", "{name...}", or "{$}".

METHOD, HOST and PATH are all optional; that is, the string can be "/".
If METHOD is present, it must be followed by at least one space or tab.
Wildcard names must be valid Go identifiers.
The "{$}" and "{name...}" wildcard must occur at the end of PATH.
PATH may end with a '/'.
Wildcard names in a path must be distinct.

nodes.Name: relationship
nodes.DocComment: relationship is a relationship between two patterns, p1 and p2.

nodes.Name: conflictsWith
nodes.DocComment:
conflictsWith reports whether p1 conflicts with p2, that is, whether
there is a request that both match but where neither is higher precedence
than the other.

	Precedence is defined by two rules:
	1. Patterns with a host win over patterns without a host.
	2. Patterns whose method and path is more specific win. One pattern is more
	   specific than another if the second matches all the (method, path) pairs
	   of the first and more.

If rule 1 doesn't apply, then two patterns conflict if their relationship
is either equivalence (they match the same set of requests) or overlap
(they both match some requests, but neither is more specific than the other).

nodes.Name: compareMethods
nodes.DocComment:
compareMethods determines the relationship between the method
part of patterns p1 and p2.

A method can either be empty, "GET", or something else.
The empty string matches any method, so it is the most general.
"GET" matches both GET and HEAD.
Anything else matches only itself.

nodes.Name: comparePaths
nodes.DocComment:
comparePaths determines the relationship between the path
part of two patterns.

nodes.Name: compareSegments
nodes.DocComment: compareSegments determines the relationship between two segments.

nodes.Name: combineRelationships
nodes.DocComment:
combineRelationships determines the overall relationship of two patterns
given the relationships of a partition of the patterns into two parts.

For example, if p1 is more general than p2 in one way but equivalent
in the other, then it is more general overall.

Or if p1 is more general in one way and more specific in the other, then
they overlap.

nodes.Name: inverseRelationship
nodes.DocComment:
If p1 has relationship `r` to p2, then
p2 has inverseRelationship(r) to p1.

nodes.Name: describeConflict
nodes.DocComment: describeConflict returns an explanation of why two patterns conflict.

nodes.Name: writeMatchingPath
nodes.DocComment: writeMatchingPath writes to b a path that matches the segments.

nodes.Name: commonPath
nodes.DocComment:
commonPath returns a path that both p1 and p2 match.
It assumes there is such a path.

nodes.Name: differencePath
nodes.DocComment:
differencePath returns a path that p1 matches and p2 doesn't.
It assumes there is such a path.
